text:
maria: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert — high GPU paging + OOM traces on r-infer-22. Observed p50 latency jump for /generate around 12:03 UTC. Starting live triage, tagging oncall. logs: https://logs.internal/r-infer-22 (access granted to SRE/RT).

pagerduty-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0471. Severity P1. Escalation: oncall-eric.

eric: I'm on it, joining. maria, can you drop a quick timeline of what you saw?

maria: timeline so far:
- 11:57 UTC: small memory jitter, a few KV evictions reported
- 11:59 UTC: burst in batch sizes from customer A (spike in concurrent requests)
- 12:01 UTC: sustained KV cache growth observed in GC log
- 12:03 UTC: first paging warnings, host swap activity up 3x
- 12:05 UTC: OOM on worker0, restarted by kube (OOMKilled)

ashwin: key hypothesis: kvcache growth + sudden larger batch arrivals -> exceeding soft-limit causing page walks. Did we change batching or scheduling recently?

maria: no config change in prod. but we had a routing bump for hosted-preview that allowed bursts.

julie: sharing GPU mem stats from the node (samples):
```
Timestamp    GPU0_free    GPU0_used    KV_cache_bytes    Process_count
11:58:50     22GB         10GB         6.1GB             4
12:02:12     6.2GB        26GB         18.4GB            9
12:04:58     2.1GB        30GB         23.0GB            11
```
Looks like KV cache dominated once concurrent requests rose.

ashwin: can we try immediate mitigation: drop max_batch_size for that model pool to 1 and force kvcache eviction? Will that stop paging?

eric: doing a live config push to the pool (rpool-a). command:
```
kubectl set env deploy/infer-pool -n hosted POOL_MAX_BATCH=1 --record
```
Applying now.

ops-bot: Config rollout started to infer-pool (hosted). 3/3 pods updated.

maria: after the change, paging rate down ~70% within 40s, no new OOMs so far. p50 latency for /generate rose ~5% but stable.

olivia-cs: Customer A reported a handful of 500s during the blast window (approx 12:00–12:06). Sent proactive note. No wider customer impact noted yet.

julie: pulled diagnostic dump from worker0 before restart and uploaded: https://artifacts.internal/oom-dumps/r-infer-22/3851234567/dump.tgz
Key excerpt from memtrack:
```
KVCache::total_entries=1.2M
KVCache::total_bytes=23,041,832,192
BatchAlloc::avg_seq_len=512
RPC inflight=18
```

ashwin: hypothesis 1: KV cache isn't cap-limited for this model variant when concurrency spikes; eviction policy too lazy. Hypothesis 2: a pathologically long sequence + larger batch pushed process over allocation peak.

maria: quick patch candidate — cap KVCACHE_BYTES to 16GB for this pool and enable more aggressive eviction (LRU window shrink). Can someone run a canary?

eric: I'll run a canary on a single pod in the pool. tagging @julie to watch metrics.

julie: canary started on infer-pod-7. New env set: KV_CACHE_LIMIT_BYTES=17179869184, KV_EVICT_WINDOW=0.8. Observing memory:
- 12:11:10 GPU0_free 14.8GB
- 12:12:05 GPU0_free 13.9GB
No paging spikes during initial 5m.

olivia-cs: updated affected customer with rollback/mitigation note. They confirm errors stopped after ~12:06.

maria: action items captured inline:
1) Short term (live): keep POOL_MAX_BATCH=1, KV_CACHE_LIMIT_BYTES=16GB via rollout to pool (owned by ashwin).
2) Mid term (post-incident RCA): enforce soft limits + backpressure on routing to avoid sudden burst.
3) Follow-up: add alert for KV cache % of GPU memory > 60% AND paging > threshold.

ashwin: rolling the KV cap to remaining pods now.

ops-bot: Rollout to infer-pool complete: 6/6 pods updated.

eric: handing off to eng-runtime for RCA writeup. Assigning to ashwin + julie. I'll mark incident as mitigated.

maria: +1. Posting final useful logs for RCA: aggregated timeline: https://logs.internal/aggregate/3851234567/timeline.txt, GPU traces: https://traces.internal/gpu/3851234567.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-2026-0471 status changed to Mitigated by eric at 12:20 UTC.

ashwin: notes for RCA: include batch arrival distribution, routing event at 11:58–12:00, check if preview routing should have rate limit. Also test kvcache cap under synthetic spike.

julie: I'll synthesize a short repro plan and run local stress with seq_len=512, concurrency=20 to validate cap triggers eviction before paging.

maria: creating postmortem ticket: PMT-824. Assigned: ashwin, julie. Due EOD tomorrow.

eric: thanks team. tagging for follow-up: @olivia-cs for customer comms follow-through. Closing live thread.
